unitAI-kmbb9.description:
## PROBLEM
XTRM-93 N2B (commit 4fbc4a30) fixed sp ps reading a retired event family, but the
same call site still passes `limit: 1000`, which is a ROW cap and not a per-job
cap. One large activation therefore consumes the entire window and every other
native activation becomes invisible.

Confirmed live against the canonical DB (<git-common-root>/.specialists/db/observability.db):

  act:51b14a21-af0   holds 1255 rows  (alone fills the 1000-row window)
  act:758931b7-9ce   holds  759 rows  -> ABSENT from `sp ps` output
  act:47a2b74f-a25                    -> ABSENT from `sp ps` output

`sp ps --json` after the fix returns exactly ONE native_activations entry, the
newest. Before the fix it returned 40 (all stale). So the change trades
"40 stale entries" for "1 current entry". That is progress on correctness but it
is NOT legacy parity: the legacy job list shows all recent jobs.

## SECONDARY EFFECT
`event_count` and `turns` are computed over the returned window, so they are
window counts rather than totals whenever the window is filled. N2B reported the
N2B activation itself as `1000 events / 72 turns` when its true counts are
`1255 / 87`. The numbers look authoritative and are silently short. Any consumer
dashboarding these will under-report.

## WHY IT IS NOT FIXED IN N2B
It is a distinct defect from the one N2B was scoped to fix, it was not known when
that contract was written, and resolving it needs a design decision that the
contract did not carry (see options).

## SCOPE
Owns: the native-activation read path in src/cli/ps.ts and whatever query
capability src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts must expose to support it,
plus tests.

## NON_GOALS
Do not change legacy (non act:) ps behaviour. Do not change the sp ps output
SHAPE. Do not re-open the retired event_family='activation' vocabulary. Do not
touch src/cli/result.ts (N2A) or src/specialist/supervisor.ts /
status-contract.ts (N0).

## CONSTRAINTS
The table is ~760k rows in a 1.5 GB database; any solution must stay index-backed
on job_id (see the EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN evidence in N2B) and must not scan.

## VALIDATION
Must demonstrate that at least the most recent N native activations are visible
regardless of how many rows any single one of them holds, and must state clearly
whether event_count/turns are totals or window counts. Include a live
demonstration showing act:758931b7-9ce and act:47a2b74f-a25 visible alongside
act:51b14a21-af0.

## OUTPUT
Design chosen and why; files changed; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN; live before/after
showing multiple activations; and an explicit statement of any remaining case
where the output is misleading.

## CANDIDATE DESIGNS (not prescriptive - decide from evidence)
  a) per-job row budget: fetch each recent act: job's newest row(s) rather than
     the newest rows overall (e.g. resolve recent act: ids first, then query per id);
  b) derive the activation list from specialist_jobs (which holds one row per
     activation, 203 act: rows) and query forensic rows only for detail;
  c) raise or make configurable the limit and paginate.

Option (b) is worth measuring first: it is the store that already has exactly one
row per activation.
unitAI-kmbb9.notes:
XTRM-93 reconciliation, base 20b888b4, 2026-09-16. Decision: option B - defect REMAINS OPEN as an N2 residual; sp ps is NOT to be recorded as full parity.

FALSIFIER, measured on the real canonical shared DB (/home/dawid/dev/specialists/.specialists/db/observability.db, not a fixture). Query used is the reader's exact plan: WHERE job_id >= 'act:' AND job_id < 'act:'||char(0xffff) ORDER BY t DESC, seq DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1000.

  distinct activations present in the global LIMIT 1000 window : 1  (act:9aeabf76-262, 1000 rows)
  distinct act: ids that actually have rows in the DB          : 249
  rows in just the newest 3 activations                        : 1591 + 765 + 2006 = 4362
  newest 10 activations by newest row                          : act:9aeabf76-262 1591, act:1dbad5f7-935 765, act:51b14a21-af0 2006, act:47a2b74f-a25 1053, act:e4dafce4-6e2 719, act:d2c877da-9ca 102, act:edb6af5c-224 24, act:758931b7-9ce 759, act:24f3233c-c40 1, act:104d7342-491 1

So 'latest 1000 events' returns 1 of 249 activations, while 'latest N activations' would return at least the 10 above. The two are not the same query and must not be described as if they were.

The strongest evidence that this is an artifact of row density rather than a property of the data: the SAME command was observed returning 3 activations earlier in this session (483/416/101 rows) and returns 1 now. sp ps enumeration therefore varies with how many rows recent activations happened to emit, not with how many activations exist. An operator cannot tell a quiet system from a hidden one.

Consequence for XTRM-93: the sp ps capability row(s) must carry this as a residual/NATIVE_GAP, NOT as PARITY or resolved. Do not close on the strength of 'the stale family and order fixes landed'. Those fixes are correct and were independent defects; they do not bound this one.

Not fixed in this pass: a correct fix is an activation-oriented projection whose LIMIT applies to activation IDs (find newest N act: ids by MAX(t), then read each activation's own window), not to raw event rows. That is a real feature change and is deliberately out of the reconciliation scope.
FOURTH observation (XTRM-93 reconciliation, base 20b888b4) - the enumeration count across observations in this single session has been 1, 3, 1, 2 activations, with no code change between them. The two most recent were act:73cb31f6-65c (376 window rows) and act:841fbe3a-c97 (624 window rows) = exactly 1000, i.e. the window was FULL and therefore truncated. act:9aeabf76-262, which had been the ONLY activation visible at the previous observation, is now not shown at all.

This is the property that makes the defect operationally serious rather than cosmetic: the operator-facing answer to 'what is running' changes with how chatty recent activations happen to be, not with what is actually running. A quiet activation is indistinguishable from an absent one, and no error or truncation marker is emitted at this level.
